added_claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
added_claims.quote: if you invested a manager you had a bad experience with it 3 years ago and and the decision was to get out of the space entirely your view is going to be completely different
added_claims.claim: Allocators' views of managed futures depend heavily on their own past experience: one bad manager experience often leads to exiting the whole space, while others internalise the strategy or move to QIS.
added_claims.testable: no - allocator decision history is not observable

added_claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
added_claims.quote: people think we are very strange for being proud of not changing what we do in eight plus years
added_claims.claim: In contrast to managers who sell a 'we changed the system and it works' story, Beer keeps his replication process unchanged for eight-plus years and treats that stability as a virtue.
added_claims.testable: partly - live record since an unchanged-process date can be evaluated out of sample

added_claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
added_claims.quote: if you want to sell that to retail I'm not sure it's still regarded as it's still regarded as complex because the underlying investment is is seen as complex
added_claims.claim: Capital-guaranteed CTA notes may also have faded because retail regulation still classes them as complex products, since the underlying strategy is seen as complex despite the guarantee.
added_claims.testable: no - regulatory classification, not a market series

added_claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
added_claims.quote: nobody's spending a lot of time analyzing the all-in cost of these things they can charge huge commissions on it
added_claims.claim: Principal-protected products sold to wealthy clients (e.g. in Latin America) are loaded with fees and commissions whose all-in cost buyers rarely analyse, which gives them a poor reputation.
added_claims.testable: partly - all-in cost of structured notes can be computed from term sheets

added_claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
added_claims.quote: we want to do 300 million but we want to put up 100 million of you know we want to manage the bond portfolio
added_claims.claim: Large institutions now unbundle guaranteed structures: they take a managed futures program at e.g. 300 million notional on 100 million of margin and manage the bond/collateral portfolio themselves, getting the same result without a stapled bond.
added_claims.conditions: institutions able to run their own collateral

added_claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
added_claims.quote: they'll pick one of the five probably not the best because he might be a little bit too crazy probably not the worst
added_claims.claim: For ease, social validation and career risk, allocators choose among the five largest managers in a space and typically pick a middle one (not the best, not the worst) rather than evaluating the full universe.
added_claims.testable: partly - flows by manager size and performance rank

added_claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
added_claims.quote: it kind of fed into this narrative of ah the reason was because they're mutual funds it was a mistake to go look for liquidity
added_claims.claim: The poor liquid-alts record was wrongly blamed on the liquid (mutual fund) wrapper, when the real cause was traditional managers pushing high-fee products they did not know how to run.
added_claims.testable: partly - compare liquid-alt returns by sponsor type and fee level

added_claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
added_claims.quote: somebody can calculate exactly how much of the heating oil Market you represent or something okay that gets a little bit scary from a front running perspective
added_claims.claim: Daily position transparency in an ETF is a real front-running risk only for very large managers whose share of a market can be calculated; for most CTAs the ETF wrapper is not a handicap.
added_claims.conditions: large manager with sizeable share of a futures market
added_claims.testable: partly - trading costs around ETF rebalance dates

added_claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
added_claims.quote: the the CTA s CTA trending it's down 11 they're down four right
added_claims.claim: Since AlphaSimplex launched its managed futures ETF, the SG CTA trend index fell about 11% while the ETF fell about 4%, evidence that an ETF need not lack risk controls.
added_claims.indicator: SG CTA Trend index vs AlphaSimplex managed futures ETF
added_claims.testable: yes - compare returns since ETF launch

added_claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
added_claims.quote: they expect a higher sharp because you've got Trend and other strategies and trading more Market market
added_claims.claim: The usual argument (put by the host) is that a fund combining trend with other strategies and more markets should, all else equal, have a higher Sharpe than a pure-trend ETF; Beer disputes that complexity adds much Sharpe.
added_claims.testable: yes - compare Sharpe of diversified vs pure-trend CTA products

added_claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
added_claims.quote: I think investors can stomach more volatility to a certain point
added_claims.claim: Replicating pre-incentive-fee returns makes the product more volatile than net-of-fee CTA indices, which Beer argues investors can accept up to a point in exchange for the higher return.
added_claims.testable: partly - compare volatility of replicators vs CTA indices

completeness_estimate: 0.85 - core macro/bond and replication claims caught; misses were mostly secondary industry/structuring points (unbundled guarantees, front-running, ETF-vs-index numbers, allocator behaviour).
